focus: Ordinary saved-data mean

turns.student: My homework scores were six, eight, and ten.
What did I average?

focus: Sort an odd list for the median

turns.student: Put down nine, two, seven, one, and four.
Which number is in the middle once they are sorted?

focus: Average the middle pair

turns.student: My times were two, four, eight, and ten.
What is the median of those?

focus: Repeated value as mode

turns.student: I got three, five, three, seven, and three.
Which one came up most?

focus: Range crossing zero

turns.student: The temperatures were negative four, two, and seven.
How far apart are the highest and lowest?

focus: Sum rather than mean

turns.student: I saved five dollars, twelve dollars, and three dollars.
How much altogether?

focus: Count observations including duplicates

turns.student: Write two, two, two, and nine.
How many results is that, including repeats?

focus: Minimum with all negative data

turns.student: Use negative eight, negative two, and negative five.
Which is the lowest?

focus: Maximum is the least negative

turns.student: My changes were negative nine, negative one, and negative four.
Which change was biggest?

focus: Population divisor is n

turns.student: The whole class has values two, four, and six.
What is the population variance?

focus: Sample divisor is n minus one

turns.student: This sample is two, four, and six.
What is the sample variance?

focus: Population standard deviation of symmetric data

turns.student: The entire group is one, three, one, three.
What is the population standard deviation?

focus: Sample standard deviation with exact square root

turns.student: My sample is two, four, and six.
What is the sample standard deviation?

focus: Upper outlier identification

turns.student: Use four, five, five, six, seven, eight, and twenty two.
Is anything an outlier?

focus: All equal values have zero range

turns.student: Every result was seven: seven, seven, seven.
What is the range if they are all equal?

focus: Signed observations cancel

turns.student: My scores changed by negative six, zero, and six.
What is the average change?

focus: Decimal values survive transcription

turns.student: Put down one point five, two point five, and nine point five.
What is the median?

focus: Zeros count as actual observations

turns.student: My results are zero, zero, four, and eight.
Count all of them, even the zeros.

focus: Negative repeated value

turns.student: Use negative two, three, negative two, and five.
What is the mode?

focus: Median survives extreme tails

turns.student: Write negative one hundred, three, four, five, and one hundred.
What is the median of that list?

focus: Decimal sum rather than concatenation

turns.student: I walked one point two, two point three, and three point five miles.
How many miles in total?

focus: Zero is the minimum in nonnegative data

turns.student: Write zero, five, and ten.
What is the smallest value?

focus: Middle pair consists of duplicates

turns.student: Use one, four, four, and twelve.
What is the median with those two fours?

focus: Sum is negative

turns.student: My changes were negative three, negative four, and two.
What is the total change?

focus: Mean and median differ on skewed data

turns.student: My results were one, two, and twelve.
First tell me the average.
And the median, for the same list?

focus: Replace a misheard final observation

turns.student: Those are six, eight, and ninety.
Wait, the last one was nine, not ninety.
What is the total now?

focus: Append an omitted observation

turns.student: My results were two and four.
I forgot six. Add that to the list.
What is the average now?

focus: Remove one erroneous observation

turns.student: Write one, three, three, and nine.
There should only be one three. Use one, three, and nine.
How many results now?

focus: A new list replaces the old list

turns.student: Use one, two, three.
New question. My list is ten, twenty, thirty.
What is the median of the new one?

focus: Correct sign without changing other observations

turns.student: Use two, four, and six.
The first one should be negative two. Keep the others.
What is the sum after that fix?

focus: Correct a decimal place

turns.student: Put down fifteen, two point five, and four.
I said one point five for the first one.
What is the total of the corrected list?

focus: Explicit reordering retains duplicate observations

turns.student: Write five, one, five, three.
Put them in order: one, three, five, five.
How many values did we keep?

focus: Explicitly remove the outlier rather than auto-filter

turns.student: Use two, three, three, four, four, five, forty.
Use the list without forty now.
What is the range now?

focus: Scale the list rather than multiply the mean alone

turns.student: My list is one, two, three.
Double every result, so use two, four, six.
What is the sum after doubling?

focus: Translate all observations

turns.student: Put down one, two, three.
Add five to each of those: six, seven, eight.
What is the range after that?

focus: Switch statistical formula without replacing data

turns.student: This is a sample: two, four, six.
What is the sample variance?
Now treat those as the whole population. What is the population variance?

focus: Distinguish variance from its square root

turns.student: Use two, four, six.
What is the sample variance first?
And the sample standard deviation?

focus: Follow total with average on unchanged list

turns.student: I read four, six, and eight pages.
How many pages total?
How many pages per day on average?

focus: Follow upper endpoint with spread

turns.student: My measurements are three, eight, eleven.
What is the maximum?
And the range, not just the highest?

focus: Switch from frequency to order

turns.student: Use two, five, five, eight.
What is the most common value?
Now which one is the smallest?

focus: Distinguish number of results from their total

turns.student: Put down three, three, six.
What is the sum?
How many numbers did I give you?

focus: Report all equally frequent modes instead of choosing one

turns.student: My results were two, two, seven, seven, and nine.
Which number came up most? If they tie, tell me both.

focus: Retain signs across two extrema queries

turns.student: Use negative ten, negative four, negative two.
Which value is lowest?
And the highest?

focus: Equal data under two spread formulas

turns.student: Everything was five: five, five, five.
What is the population variance?
What about the population standard deviation?

focus: Mean and count for a two-observation list

turns.student: My two results were ten and fourteen.
What is the average of those two?
How many observations are there?

focus: Reordering does not change the even median

turns.student: Use ten, two, eight, four.
Reorder those as two, four, eight, ten.
What is the median?

focus: Repeats are not accidental deduplication

turns.student: Put down two, four, eight.
Actually four happened twice. Use two, four, four, eight.
What is the mode now?

focus: Replace a negative value with zero

turns.student: Use negative two, four, six.
Change the negative two to zero.
What is the minimum now?

focus: Use only observed values after a mistaken placeholder

turns.student: Use zero, four, eight.
The zero was missing, not a real result. Use four and eight.
What is the average of the actual results?

focus: Query does not sort the saved input list

turns.student: Write eight, one, five in that order.
Tell me the median, but leave my list alone.
Give me a summary of that list, but keep my order.

focus: Temporary statistics must not replace an equation

turns.student: Write x plus three equals eight.
Quick side question: what is the average of two, four, and nine?
Now subtract three on both sides of my equation.

focus: A temporary list query preserves graph

turns.student: Graph x squared.
What is the median of two, four, eight, and ten?
Back to the graph. What is y when x is three?

focus: Temporary total preserves dimensions

turns.student: Draw a rectangle four wide and three high.
What do two, five, and eight add up to?
What is the area of my rectangle?

focus: Solving an unrelated equation leaves saved list

turns.student: Keep these results: two, four, six.
Can you solve x plus five equals nine without replacing this?
What is the average of my results?

focus: Calculation does not replace dataset

turns.student: My numbers are three, six, nine.
What is seven times eight?
And what was the median of my numbers?

focus: Explicitly switch from equation to statistics

turns.student: Write two x equals twelve.
New problem. Record four, six, eight.
What is the mean of these?

focus: Equation replaces visible statistics

turns.student: Use two, five, eight.
Now write x minus two equals seven.
Solve that equation.

focus: The latest dataset wins over a graph reference

turns.student: Graph x plus one.
Switch to these measurements: five, seven, nine.
How many measurements?

focus: Plot an explicit relation after statistics

turns.student: Put down one, four, nine.
Now graph y equals x squared.
Read the graph at x equals two.

focus: Shape work followed by numeric observations

turns.student: Draw a rectangle five by two.
Now my data is two, three, ten.
What is its median?

focus: Switch to geometry and measure the new object

turns.student: Record two, four, six.
Draw a circle with radius three.
What is the diameter?

focus: New geometry does not edit equation coefficients

turns.student: Write three x equals fifteen.
Different question: draw a rectangle six by two.
What is its perimeter?

focus: Equation after a shape uses the equation context

turns.student: Draw a square with side four.
Write x plus four equals ten.
Solve this one.

focus: Draw means different representations by context

turns.student: Draw a circle with radius two.
Now draw the graph of y equals two x.
What is the graph value at three?

focus: Geometry becomes current after graphing

turns.student: Show y equals x.
Now draw a right triangle with legs three and four.
How long is the hypotenuse?

focus: Count inline observations without saving

turns.student: Draw a rectangle eight by three.
How many numbers are in two, two, five, nine?
Read the area of the rectangle again.

focus: Signed range side question

turns.student: Write x minus four equals one.
What is the range of negative three, zero, and five?
Now solve the equation I kept.

focus: Numeric maximum is not graph maximum

turns.student: Graph x squared minus four.
Which number is biggest: negative two, three, or one?
Where is my graph at zero?

focus: Arithmetic before returning to a shape

turns.student: Circle, radius five.
What is twenty divided by four?
And the diameter of that circle?

focus: An equation answer must not overwrite a graph

turns.student: Graph y equals three x.
Solve x minus seven equals two as a side question.
And read the graph at two.

focus: Inline list and saved list are separate

turns.student: My actual list is ten, twenty, thirty.
What is the median of just one, two, and nine?
Now the median of my saved list?

focus: Temporary sample leaves population observations

turns.student: Keep five, five, five.
What is the sample variance of two, four, six?
And the population variance of my saved values?

focus: Repeated inline queries do not leak state

turns.student: Write x equals three.
What is the sum of two and eight?
And the median of four, six, eight?
Read my equation again.

focus: Spoken units do not enter statistic expressions

turns.student: I ran three minutes, five minutes, and seven minutes.
What is my average time?
And my total time?

focus: Recalculate population variance after replacing data

turns.student: Use one, three, one, three.
What is the population variance?
Now every result is two. Use two, two, two, two.
What is the population variance now?

focus: Undo restores the earlier dataset

turns.student: Use two, four, six.
Replace those with ten, twenty, thirty.
Undo that last change.
What is the mean of the restored list?

focus: Redo restores the newer dataset

turns.student: Use two, four, six.
Use ten, twenty, thirty instead.
Undo that last change.
Put that change back.
What is the mean now?

focus: A read-only statistic does not consume undo

turns.student: Use one, two, three.
Change them to four, five, six.
What is the mean?
Undo that last change.
Read the mean now.

focus: Undo returns from geometry to dataset

turns.student: Use two, four, six.
Draw a rectangle three by four.
Undo that last change.
What is the median of my list again?

focus: Redo restores a shape after switching modes

turns.student: Put down one, two, three.
Draw a square with side five.
Undo that last change.
Put that change back.
What is the area of the square?

focus: Clearing is recoverable

turns.student: Save three, six, nine.
Clear this problem.
Undo that last change.
What is the sum now that it is back?

focus: Undo count applies whole requests

turns.student: Start with one, two, three.
Change to four, five, six.
Now seven, eight, nine.
Undo those last two changes.
Which average are we back to?

focus: Redo multiple complete requests

turns.student: Use one, two, three.
Now four, five, six.
Then seven, eight, nine.
Undo twice.
Redo both changes.
What is the average again?

focus: New edit after undo branches from restored data

turns.student: Use one, two, three.
Change to four, five, six.
Undo that last change.
Use one, two, three, four instead.
How many observations on this version?

focus: Clear then undo restores an equation

turns.student: Write x plus two equals seven.
Clear it.
Undo that last change.
Solve the one we restored.

focus: Record a student procedure in order

turns.student: Make a flow: start, add three, divide by two, finish.
Read the steps back.

focus: Change one named operation

turns.student: My flow is start, multiply by two, stop.
Change multiply by two to multiply by three.
Read it now.

focus: Undo restores the former operation label

turns.student: Make start, add two, finish.
Replace add two with subtract two.
Undo that last change.
Read the flow after undo.

focus: Redo reapplies a text edit

turns.student: Show input, square it, output.
Change square it to cube it.
Undo that last change.
Put that change back.
What are the steps now?

focus: Rename a checklist step using a natural spoken label

turns.student: Make start, check answer, finish.
Change check answer to check my units.
Read that back.

focus: A new procedure replaces old steps

turns.student: Make input, double, output.
New flow: input, subtract one, square, output.
Read the new one.

focus: A calculation leaves diagram unchanged

turns.student: Show start, add seven, finish.
What is seven plus eight?
Read my flow again.

focus: A new equation becomes current after a flow

turns.student: Make start, double, finish.
Now write two x equals eighteen.
Solve this.

focus: Represent the next problem as a procedure

turns.student: Write x equals four.
Now show a flow: input, add four, output.
Read that procedure.

focus: Undo restores the entire old procedure

turns.student: Start, add five, finish.
Use start, subtract five, finish instead.
Undo that last change.
Which flow is back?

focus: Two consecutive edits refer to the latest labels

turns.student: Input, add two, divide by three, output.
Change add two to add four.
And change divide by three to divide by two.
Read both changes.

focus: Replace middle step without losing adjacent steps

turns.student: Start, add two, check units, finish.
Change check units to check the sign.
Read all the steps.

focus: Clear recoverably retains procedural work

turns.student: Make input, halve, output.
Clear that.
Undo that last change.
Read the restored procedure.

focus: Temporary mean cannot overwrite flow steps

turns.student: Make start, collect results, finish.
What is the average of three, six, and nine?
Back to the flow. Read it.

focus: Undo a representation change returns to observations

turns.student: Keep two, five, eight.
Show collect data, find mean, report.
Undo that last change.
What is the mean of my data?
